briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The conflict between the United States and Iran escalated significantly over the past 24 hours, with the US completing its 11th consecutive night of strikes against Iranian military infrastructure across multiple provinces, while Iran launched retaliatory missile and drone attacks on US bases in Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait. Concurrently, former President Trump formally approved a landmark 30-year civilian nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia, decoupling it from Israel normalization, amid ongoing Houthi maritime threats impacting Red Sea shipping.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran intensified, with the US Central Command (CENTCOM) confirming its 11th consecutive night of strikes, targeting military operations centers, naval capabilities, drone storage, aircraft hangars, and logistical infrastructure across Iran. Reported strike locations include Tabriz (East Azerbaijan), Mahshahr, Bushehr, Sirik (Hormozgan), Behbehan (Khuzestan - Bekhradian Barracks, Bidboland Refinery), Omidiyeh (Khuzestan), Parsian (Tehran), Chabahar, Konarak (Sistan and Baluchestan), Khorramabad, Kangavar (Kermanshah), Baneh (Kordestan), Kabudarahang and Nojeh Airbase (Hamedan), and areas in Ilam (Chavar, Abdanan, Anarak, Dinarkuh). Iranian state media, Press TV, reported that US attacks specifically targeted civilian infrastructure in southern Iran.

In retaliation, Iran launched missile and drone attacks. Jordan reported intercepting two missiles and five drones, while Iran claimed these targeted the US Al-Azraq Air Base. Bahrain experienced alarms and reports of direct hits, with Iran claiming to have struck Sheikh Isa Air Base. Kuwait's Al-Doha Camp was reportedly targeted by Iranian drones, with Kuwaiti air defenses active. A US soldier, Sergeant Angel S. Rambersad, was reported killed, having been previously missing after an Iranian attack on a US base in Jordan.

Internally, Iran's Khatam al-AnbiYa Headquarters issued a stern warning that any US attack on Iranian nuclear or vital sites would be considered an "expansion of war" and would result in powerful retaliation against all US, allied, and supporter interests. President Pezeshkian emphasized strengthening ties with the Supreme Leader and adherence to his guidance in negotiations. Communication infrastructure in Khuzestan Province was reportedly hit, disrupting connectivity to Qeshm and Kharg Islands, requiring temporary reliance on radio and satellite. Iran executed one individual, Mehdi Khannaki, accused of participating in January protests and acting for Israel and the US.

ISRAEL
Israel experienced indirect impacts of the regional escalation, with distant explosions heard and smoke seen in Eilat, originating from missile attacks on Aqaba, Jordan. An Arkia flight to Eilat was diverted. No missile penetrations into Israeli territory were reported from the Iranian launches.

On the military front, the IDF announced the killing of several armed Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) operatives and other gunmen in the southern Gaza Strip. Additionally, the IDF eliminated Hamas commander Asma Kamal Shahada Abu Tim in southern Gaza, who was implicated in the October 7th Nir Oz kidnapping of Nurit Cooper, Amiram Cooper, and Alexander Danzig. Along the Lebanese border, IDF forces fired warning shots into the air after Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) soldiers and heavy machinery crossed approximately 150 meters into Israel's security zone in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, breaching barriers, in violation of existing understandings. Colonel D assumed command of the Shomron Brigade.

Politically, President Isaac Herzog delivered a statement ahead of Tisha B'Av, appealing for national unity and caution against incitement during the upcoming election period, citing warnings from the Shin Bet about threats to election integrity. The Prosecutor's Office, at PM Netanyahu's request, submitted a request for the unprecedented revocation of citizenship for two security prisoners who aided Hamas, citing breach of loyalty.

Economically, Monday.com, an Israeli tech company, announced a significant layoff of 20% of its workforce (620 employees). Oil prices climbed, potentially impacting the Israeli economy. Air India extended its suspension of flights to Tel Aviv until October 2026, and US airlines are not expected to resume flights before September, reflecting ongoing security concerns. Nauru announced it would open an embassy in Jerusalem.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Ground operations in Gaza saw the IDF eliminate several armed Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) operatives and other gunmen in the southern Gaza Strip. A key Hamas commander, Asma Kamal Shahada Abu Tim, was killed in an IDF strike in southern Gaza. Abu Tim was identified as a participant in the October 7th attack on Kibbutz Nir Oz and the kidnapping of Nurit Cooper, Amiram Cooper, and Alexander Danzig. He was also involved in planning terror attacks against IDF forces and Israeli civilians.

Regarding the humanitarian situation, US Senator Bernie Sanders publicly stated that Israel "did not have the right to commit genocide" in Gaza and should not receive additional US taxpayer money. Ceasefire efforts remain stalled, with former President Trump reportedly rejecting a 10-day ceasefire proposal from Qatar and Pakistan. There was no direct reporting on new settler activity in the West Bank, but the new commander of the Shomron Brigade was noted.

LEBANON
The Lebanese Prime Minister, Nawaf Salam, visited the village of Zawtar al-Gharbiya, a location where the IDF recently withdrew as part of a pilot program to return control to the Beirut government. Along the southern border, an incident occurred where Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) soldiers and heavy machinery crossed approximately 150 meters into Israel's security zone in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, breaching barriers, contrary to understandings. IDF forces responded by firing warning shots into the air, causing the LAF contingent to withdraw without injuries. The LAF subsequently reported that Israeli forces fired near their units during their deployment, which they claimed could delay the pilot program's implementation. Former President Trump announced that he would allow US airlines to operate direct flights to Lebanon following a meeting with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Iraq, three explosive drones were intercepted near the US Consulate, indicating continued threats to US interests. Explosions were reported in Sulaymaniyah, northern Iraq, and specifically in Halabja, targeting camps of Iranian opposition groups. Satellite imagery reportedly showed damage to a ground support station and maintenance facility for US surveillance aircraft at Erbil International Airport, following Iranian missile strikes. A US Air Force E-11A communications aircraft was observed heading to Ramstein Air Base, likely for deployment to Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia.

In Syria, intensified clashes were reported between the Qasd militia and Golani gangs in Hasaka. The Syrian regime announced the interception of a vehicle attempting to smuggle 226 small bombs into Lebanese territory.

GULF STATES
Former President Trump formally approved a landmark 30-year civilian nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia, valued at tens of billions of dollars. This agreement is designed to provide Saudi Arabia with a civilian nuclear program and potentially allow for uranium enrichment on Saudi soil by American companies, effectively separating this development from the condition of Saudi recognition and normalization with Israel.

The Houthi maritime blockade targeting Saudi ports escalated, with reports of emails warning shipping companies against docking in Saudi Arabia, leading to at least six commercial vessels, including cargo ships and oil tankers, redirecting their courses away from Saudi ports like Yanbu. Saudi Arabia's crude oil exports reportedly hit a record low in May due to the US-Iran conflict and shipping disruptions.

Kuwait reported its air defense systems actively intercepting Iranian drones following "blatant Iranian aggression." Kuwait also summoned the Iranian ambassador to protest a recent Iranian attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain experienced air raid alarms and reports of direct hits from Iranian missile strikes, with Sheikh Isa Air Base reportedly targeted by Iran.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with CENTCOM reporting that Iran has attacked over 30 commercial vessels in the past three months, while US forces have secured the passage of approximately 900 commercial ships and 450 million barrels of crude oil since early May. Despite this, CENTCOM maintains the Strait remains open for commercial shipping. Goldman Sachs estimates indicate a gradual reduction in oil export reliance on the Strait, with about 5 million barrels per day increasingly using alternative pipelines and land routes. Oil prices, specifically Brent crude, climbed to $92-93 amid the regional tensions.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Strikes Iran:** The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the completion of its 11th consecutive night of strikes against Iranian military targets across multiple provinces, including Tabriz, Bushehr, Behbehan, Chabahar, and Hamedan.
2.  **Iran Retaliates Regionally:** Iran launched missile and drone attacks targeting US military bases in Jordan (Al-Azraq Air Base), Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base), and Kuwait (Al-Doha Camp); one US soldier, Angel S. Rambersad, is presumed killed after an earlier Iranian attack in Jordan.
3.  **Saudi Civilian Nuclear Deal:** Former President Trump formally approved a 30-year civilian nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia, valued at tens of billions, which could allow US companies to build an uranium enrichment facility in the Kingdom, decoupled from Israel normalization.
4.  **Houthi Maritime Blockade:** Houthi forces enforced a maritime blockade of Saudi ports, sending warnings to shipping companies and causing at least six commercial vessels, including oil tankers, to divert from Saudi destinations.
5.  **IDF Gaza Operations:** The IDF eliminated several armed Palestinian Islamic Jihad operatives and a Hamas commander, Asma Kamal Shahada Abu Tim, in southern Gaza, who was involved in the October 7th Nir Oz kidnapping.
6.  **IDF-LAF Border Incident:** IDF forces fired warning shots at Lebanese Armed Forces soldiers and heavy machinery that breached Israel's security zone in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah by 150 meters, violating existing understandings.
7.  **Iran's Nuclear Red Line:** Iran's Khatam al-AnbiYa Headquarters warned the US that any attack on Iranian nuclear or vital sites would be considered an "expansion of war," leading to retaliation against US, allied, and supporter interests.
8.  **Oil Price Surge:** Brent crude oil prices climbed to $92-93 per barrel amidst the escalating tensions and shipping disruptions in the Middle East.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high due to the direct and sustained military exchanges between the US and Iran. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where both sides claim control and have engaged in hostilities impacting commercial shipping, and US military bases in Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait, which are increasingly targets of Iranian retaliation. The US military posture indicates a continued offensive campaign to degrade Iran's capabilities, with US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth stating the war has already cost $37.5 billion and claiming an "effective blockade" on Iranian vessels. Iran's military posture involves retaliatory strikes and explicit red lines: its Khatam al-AnbiYa Headquarters warned that any attack on its nuclear or vital facilities would lead to a widespread response targeting all US and allied interests, a threat made more potent by Israeli intelligence reports suggesting Iran moved enriched uranium and centrifuges to deep tunnels under "Pickaxe Mountain" near Natanz. Trump's public threat to strike "Pickaxe Mountain" further heightens this risk of direct engagement on nuclear sites.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** stance is defined by continued military aggression against Iran, as articulated by CENTCOM's daily strike reports. Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed openness to talks if Iran is "serious," while also warning about the dangerous precedent of closing international shipping lanes. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth reported the war's cost at $37.5 billion and accused Russia and China of enabling Iran's actions. Former President Trump made significant policy moves, formally approving a civilian nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia, notably decoupled from Israel normalization, and publicly threatening to strike "Pickaxe Mountain" in Iran. He also stated he would allow direct US flights to Lebanon. Trump rejected a 10-day ceasefire offer from Qatar and Pakistan.

The **United Kingdom**, under new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, approved the continued use of British bases (Diego Garcia and RAF Fairford) by the US for "defensive strikes" against Iranian missile threats and actions in the Strait of Hormuz, maintaining his predecessor's policy.

The **UN** Secretary-General António Guterres expressed concern over attacks on civilian infrastructure in Iran, as reported by UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric.

**Kuwait** summoned the Iranian ambassador to protest an earlier Iranian attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz and activated its air defense systems against incoming Iranian drones.

**Pakistan**, alongside Qatar, attempted to mediate a 10-day ceasefire between the US and Iran, which was rejected by former President Trump. Pakistan's Interior Minister also met with the Chief of Army Staff to discuss renewing US-Iran negotiations.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims exist within the intelligence feed. The Hormozgan Deputy Governor denied any enemy attacks on Sirik or other parts of the province, directly contradicting reports from other sources and Iranian state media. Similarly, while Iranian state media (Press TV) claims US attacks targeted "civilian infrastructure," CENTCOM explicitly states military operations centers, maritime capabilities, and drone storage were targeted, indicating a potential propaganda effort to frame US actions as illegitimate. Iranian claims of targeting specific infrastructure like water desalination and power generation plants in Kuwait lack independent verification, with Kuwaiti officials only reporting interception of drones.

Propaganda indicators are evident in both US and Iranian reporting. Iranian state media frames its military as "heroic" and US forces as "criminal" or "aggressors," while repeatedly emphasizing the suffering of Minab schoolchildren. Former President Trump's rhetoric, including his public threats against "Pickaxe Mountain" and his branding of the Iranian regime as "savages," serves to inflame tensions and may be intended for domestic political consumption. His casual dismissal of intelligence regarding Iranian nuclear activities at "Pickaxe Mountain" as "fake news" while simultaneously threatening to strike it highlights a disconnect.

Reporting gaps include a lack of specific casualty numbers for the Iranian retaliatory strikes on US bases (beyond the one missing/presumed killed US soldier). Comprehensive, independent damage assessments for the numerous Iranian locations reportedly struck by the US are also absent, making it difficult to fully gauge the impact of the US campaign. The precise nature and efficacy of Iranian air defense systems are also difficult to ascertain, with various reports of activation and interception without clear outcomes.
